title: Singing choruses and lung damage from soldering fumes
summary: He sang choruses through paper megaphones until fumes damaged his lungs.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you sing anything? I used to sing choruses practically every song. Oh, yeah. The chorus, but since then I got, I had an accident. I inhaled some, I'm doing some soldering, and I inhaled some fumes from the soldering, and it damaged my lung to a certain extent. I go to the hospital now, but it damaged my lung to a certain extent, and I can't sing. You never did go for treatment? Yeah, I go to the hospital now. You still have to go? Oh, yeah. How long ago that happened? Oh, that happened about, maybe fifteen years ago. And it still bothers you? Yeah, occasionally I have trouble. Oh, with your breathing? I have a bad, have trouble breathing.
Oh. What happened when you get, when the accident happened? Did you get very sick right after? Well, no, I never get real sick, but... You didn't go to treatment right away?
No, it didn't go to treatment right away.
Otherwise, I had pretty good voices singing. I'd sing all the choruses.
And people liked that, they wanted you to sing? Yeah, they liked it.

How did you sing without microphones in those days? Well, I'll tell you what, we used to have a... A megaphone? Yeah, yeah. A big piece of paper pulled up like a funnel, and you sing through there. I mean, that was the only way you could spread the voice out. Like today, you've got a microphone, now you can use that. Right.
